title: Memory leak and unreadable text in Run
author: CircuitDaemon
summary: The reproducible long-query overlap is the known PowerToys Run autocomplete rendering defect; the reported memory growth is unproven by the supplied diagnostics and predates the released stale-query worker-lifetime fix.

status.label: Current-release memory retest needed
status.detail: Do not create a competing UI fix until the canonical visual tracker is resolved; retest the separate memory claim on current stable.

next_action.label: Request current-release Run memory retest
next_action.reason: The historic diagnostic has no reproduction-time allocation, heap, or thread evidence, and the reported version predates the shipped cancellation fix.

judgment.rationale: The exact query and screenshots establish a known visual overlap, while the memory observation is from PowerToys 0.97.2. The maintainer confirms that the later Run worker-lifetime fix covers the known memory mechanism and is included in stable 0.101.2362.0. The supplied diagnostics do not prove that mechanism caused this report, and the visual defect remains separately tracked. A current-release retest is therefore needed before any new memory fix is proposed.
evidence: The report includes an exact long query, overlap screenshots, a diagnostic archive, a text attachment, and a screenshot of high PowerToys Run memory.
Issue 13554 remains the canonical long-input autocomplete-alignment tracker.
LauncherControl.xaml overlays QueryTextBox and AutoCompleteTextBlock while the TextBox content scrolls independently.
The supplied diagnostic has no process dump, ETL, GC dump, runtime trace, thread timeline, or memory timeline; its current PowerToys Run log records startup and restart only.
PR 48394 fixed stale-query worker accumulation and is included in the latest stable 0.101.2362.0; the reported installation is 0.97.2.
A maintainer comment on 2026-09-04 directs the reporter to update because the Window Walker memory issue was fixed several months ago.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the visual symptom with Issue 13554 and request a current-stable, time-series memory and thread retest; only investigate a new memory defect if growth persists after update and dismissal.

fix_assessment.rationale: PR 48394 concretely fixes the stale-query worker accumulation mechanism that can cause Run worker and memory growth and is in the latest stable release, matching the maintainer's direction. It does not fix the separately tracked visual layout defect or prove this report used that mechanism; that portion needs a current-release retest.

issue_context.summary: A long mixed-character Run query visibly overlaps the autocomplete text; after repeated editing, the reporter observed severe memory growth on a version predating later query-worker lifetime work.
known_information: The report targets PowerToys 0.97.2 on Windows 11 build 26200.
The mixed-character query produces the visual overlap after one more character.
The issue includes a screenshot showing substantial memory attributed to PowerToys Run.
The diagnostic archive includes no heap or runtime trace establishing memory retention.
PR 48394 is merged and included in the latest stable 0.101.2362.0.
A maintainer advised updating to the latest version because the reported memory issue was fixed several months ago.
inferences: The visual symptom is another instance of Issue 13554.
The separate stationary autocomplete surface likely contributes to the visual overlap.
The memory symptom is likely covered by PR 48394, but no evidence ties this occurrence to its stale-query worker mechanism.
The visual defect and memory growth are not established as one root cause.
issue_context.analysis: The issue combines two mechanisms that must not be conflated. The visual symptom follows the existing independent autocomplete rendering path and belongs with Issue 13554. The historical memory observation may be the stale-query worker accumulation fixed after 0.97.2, consistent with the maintainer's update guidance, but the supplied archive cannot establish that. A current-release time series is the narrow evidence needed before a new memory investigation. A separate adversarial review rejected a duplicate-overlay UI change because matching offsets do not guarantee matching TextBox glyph geometry, can regress mixed-direction text, and risk exposing a second Edit control to accessibility tools.

design.root_cause: This report contains two distinct paths. The visual overlap is caused by LauncherControl rendering the full autocomplete string in the independent AutoCompleteTextBlock while QueryTextBox scrolls its own PART_ContentHost; their text origins and clipping are not shared. The historical memory allegation is not diagnosed by the archive. On the reported 0.97.2 build, MainViewModel's mutable query cancellation state could permit stale plugin queries to continue; current code replaces that lifetime with QuerySession, which captures one token per query and disposes its source only after completion.

evidence.detail: The report supplies an exact long mixed-character query and screenshots showing the visual overlap after one additional character.

LauncherControl.xaml places QueryTextBox and AutoCompleteTextBlock as sibling visuals; QueryTextBox's control template owns a horizontally scrolling PART_ContentHost while the autocomplete TextBlock has no shared scroll or viewport.

MainWindow.xaml.cs SuggestionsList_SelectionChanged writes the full completed string to AutoCompleteTextBlock, ClearAutoCompleteText clears it, and SearchBox_UpdateFlowDirection assigns each visual separately.
The diagnostic archive contains no reproduction-time heap, GC, runtime, thread, or memory timeline. Its current launcher log records normal disable, enable, and startup events, not a failure.
PR 48394 changed MainViewModel.QueryResults, added QuerySession and PluginQueryExecutionGate, and added focused Wox.Test coverage; the merge shipped in v0.101.2362.0.
The old mutable-token mechanism could explain a 0.97.2 worker-growth report, but the supplied evidence cannot attribute this report to it.

Regression coverage for the released worker-lifetime fix.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The same report combines a reproducible legacy autocomplete presentation defect and an unmeasured memory allegation.
implementation_steps.change: Do not implement a competing visual fix from this report. Keep the rendering work with the canonical visual tracker and gate a new memory fix on the current-release retest.
implementation_steps.handling: Do not close the report solely as visual duplication until the retest resolves the independent memory claim. Do not infer a heap leak from a working-set screenshot.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The pre-release implementation let stale workers read mutable cancellation state after a newer query replaced it, while disposal could race active consumers.
implementation_steps.change: No new change is proposed: retain the released QuerySession model. Each query captures its own token, prior sessions are cancelled, and CTS disposal waits for the tracked completion task.
implementation_steps.handling: Keep generation checks, per-plugin execution gating, cancellation propagation, and bounded shutdown waiting intact. A future memory fix must prove a distinct retained object or work source before modifying these lifetime guarantees.
implementation_steps.tests: Retain QuerySessionTest token ownership, deferred-disposal, timeout, and suspended-start tests; add a focused regression only after a current-build reproduction identifies a different mechanism.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The editable TextBox scrolls inside PART_ContentHost while a full autocomplete string is rendered by a separate sibling TextBlock.
implementation_steps.change: No competing pseudo-fix is approved. Independent reviews rejected offset synchronization and duplicate TextBox variants because they do not establish matching glyph geometry, fail mixed-direction text, can lose sync on content replacement, and can expose a second editable automation control.
implementation_steps.code_block: defer UI change\nrequire a canonical design that proves: rendered completion region does not intersect rendered query glyphs\nrequire: one accessible edit control, current caret/IME behavior, and production-template LTR/RTL visual tests
implementation_steps.handling: A future design may render only a safely non-intersecting completion suffix or use a shared text-layout primitive, but it must suppress ambiguous bidirectional cases rather than overlap text.

automated: Build src/modules/launcher/Wox.Test/Wox.Test.csproj with the repository's existing build workflow and run the resulting Wox.Test assembly through Visual Studio Test Explorer or vstest.console.exe.

For a future UI implementation, add an STA test that realizes the production LauncherControl template and verifies rendered nonintersection, clipping, one Edit automation peer, text clear/repopulate, resize, template replacement, LTR, RTL, and mixed-direction input.
manual: On current stable, enter the exact reported query and add one character; confirm the canonical visual tracker still captures any overlap without claiming this artifact fixes it.

Record PowerToys.PowerLauncher process ID, private bytes or private working set, and thread count at idle, peak during 10 to 15 seconds of repeated exact-query edits, immediately after clearing, immediately after dismissal, and after 60 seconds.
If elevated values persist after dismissal, submit /bugreport immediately after reproduction; otherwise do not open a new memory implementation.

risks: Treating an old-version working-set screenshot as a diagnosed leak could introduce an unnecessary and unsafe query-pipeline change.
A second autocomplete renderer can misalign at fractional DPI, after scrolling, or with mixed bidirectional text even when offsets match.
A decorative TextBox can create a duplicate Edit control for screen readers.
Closing the issue solely as a visual duplicate could discard a still-reproducible current-release memory defect.

alternatives.option: Synchronize an independent TextBlock or second TextBox with the input scroll offset.
alternatives.rejected_because: Independent adversary review found that equal offsets do not guarantee identical TextBox glyph origins, correct clipping, content-reset synchronization, mixed-direction rendering, or accessibility.

alternatives.option: Implement a new autocomplete adorner anchored at the logical end caret.
alternatives.rejected_because: Mixed bidirectional text can place a logical caret edge within visible query glyph geometry; no safe nonintersection rule was established.

alternatives.option: Treat the legacy report as fully fixed by the released worker-lifetime change.
alternatives.rejected_because: That change does not address the visual defect and the archive cannot prove it was the cause of this report's memory observation.

adversary.signoff: No blocking objections remain to the evidence-gated, non-competing disposition. Three independent critiques rejected concrete overlay and adorner implementation proposals because their geometry, mixed-direction, synchronization, and accessibility invariants were not proven.
non_blocking_notes: The canonical visual tracker needs a separate implementation-ready WPF rendering design.
A current-release memory retest must use a time series rather than a single working-set observation.
